problem: Review and maintenance audit a repo by reading a curated corpus and by judgment. They run no linter. A smell a tool can count, such as a duplicated block, is invisible to a reading pass.
approach: One script, shared/habit_smells.py, shells out to habit-sensors --branch <base> --json, groups the findings per smell and per file, and writes habit-smells.json into a --out directory. It records run_complete false with the broken tool name, and available false with a reason. Review mode adds a Mechanical smells section to both reports. Maintenance mode diffs each pair against the previous report and tags it NEW, ESCALATED, STABLE, or RESOLVED. verify_bundle gains an optional habit.smells warning.

alternatives.option: Paste the rendered habit-hooks output into the reports
alternatives.why_not: The rendered text is session coaching, not a findings record a report can diff.

alternatives.option: Let only review mode read the smells
alternatives.why_not: Maintenance needs the same scan as its baseline, or the first trend has no pair.
ADR-0025 keeps habit-hooks an external CLI. Vendoring forks its release.

risks.risk: A duplicate-code group holds hundreds of findings, so the section can flood a report.
risks.mitigation: A group over 100 findings reports one count and its top 10 files.

risks.risk: A broken tool run reads as a clean scan.
risks.mitigation: An incomplete run is a P1 finding that names the tool.

testing: Tests use a stub habit-sensors on PATH with a fixture repo. Integration tests pin the mode prose and the command files.
